stories.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OHWZ The only known remaining photo of resistance fighter Eva Mamlok Image: Familienarchiv Siemsen Advertisement In the history of German resistance to Nazism , some names have become symbols: Sophie Scholl , Claus von Stauffenberg , Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Georg Elser . Yet many others have remained largely forgotten. Among them is Eva Mamlok, a young Jewish woman from Berlin whose acts of defiance began in her teenage years and continued until her murder in a Nazi concentration camp. Now more people will get to know her story as Berlin renames Blücherplatz, a square in the district of Kreuzberg, Eva-Mamlok-Platz on October 16. "Eva Mamlok was a very remarkable person. stories.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

stories.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
stories.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

stories.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
stories.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

stories.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
stories.summary: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

stories.title: Palestinians in Gaza dread another winter with nowhere safe to shelter
stories.summary: More than 44,000 people still live in buildings marked for demolition across the territory, unable to leave because no alternative shelter exists. Euronews spoke to families in Al-Mughraqa as tarpaulin prices double and Israel blocks timber and shelter kits from entering Gaza.

stories.title: Japan's first female PM says makeup and housework add hours to her working day
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says household chores and getting ready for TV appearances add three to four hours to her working day compared with male predecessors.
